title: Triangulated closure of the rational evaluation class
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ be the completed coefficient sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $(\mathcal S,\mathcal R)$ be either $(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X})$ or the slice $(X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}|_U)$ over an object $U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $\mathcal T$ be the derived category of sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules on $\mathcal S$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], an $\mathcal O_E$-linear triangulated category, with derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the completed tensor product $\widehat\otimes^L$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], formed on $\mathcal S$ with the restricted coefficient sheaves. Let $Q:\mathcal T\to\mathcal T[1/\varpi_E]$ be the scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] with its triangulated structure [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated]. Fix $M\in\mathcal T$ derived complete in the sense of [def-weil-derived-complete] (formed on $\mathcal S$). Then the contravariant functors $\Phi(L)=R\mathcal Hom(L,\mathcal R)\widehat\otimes^L M$ and $\Psi(L)=R\mathcal Hom(L,M)$ on $\mathcal T$ are exact and $\mathcal O_E$-linear, and the canonical evaluation comparison $\theta_{L,M}:\Phi(L)\to\Psi(L)$ (the adjunct of evaluation; $\Psi(L)$ is derived complete) is natural in $L$ and compatible with the shift isomorphisms. Hence $\Phi,\Psi$ induce exact functors on $\mathcal T[1/\varpi_E]$ and $Q(\theta_{-,M})$ is a natural transformation between them compatible with shifts. The class $\mathcal S_M$ of objects $L$ for which $Q(\theta_{L,M})$ is an isomorphism in $\mathcal T[1/\varpi_E]$ contains $\mathcal R[0]$ and $0$, and is closed under isomorphisms in $\mathcal T[1/\varpi_E]$, finite direct sums, retracts in $\mathcal T[1/\varpi_E]$, shifts, and extensions: if $L_1\to L_2\to L_3\to L_1[1]$ is a distinguished triangle of $\mathcal T[1/\varpi_E]$ and two of the $L_i$ lie in $\mathcal S_M$, so does the third.

source.place: Unit proof, first paragraph: 'both constructions are exact functors of P preserving direct summands'; applied to the rational coefficient operations before the bounded-complex induction.

proof.text: Put $t=\varpi_E$, $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/t^n)_{\mathcal S}$ and $H=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal R}$. The coefficient ring $\mathcal O_E$ is Noetherian (it is a DVR), so [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] applies on $\mathcal S$: on a slice the constant finite coefficient sheaves and their inverse limit restrict sectionwise, by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. In particular $\mathcal R/t^n\mathcal R=B_n$. Let $C(A)=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(A\otimes^L_{\mathcal R}B_n)$, with the quotient unit $\eta_A:A\to C(A)$. The Koszul/quotient comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] and the universal property of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] identify $C$ with the reflector onto locally derived $(t)$-complete objects. Thus the derived completeness in the statement is this condition: its Roos triangle is the quotient-tower completion triangle, and $\eta_A$ is an isomorphism precisely on complete objects. These cited results are for arbitrary small sites, so they apply directly on the slice, without a compactness or constructibility hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 099L and 099M (proetale.tex); Tag 0A0E (algebraization.tex); quotient completion and its unit

proof.text:
Write $A\otimes^L B$ for ordinary derived tensor over $\mathcal R$. For flat-term K-flat representatives $P,Q$, the levelwise balanced tensor identification
$$ (P\otimes_{\mathcal R}B_n)\otimes_{B_n}(Q\otimes_{\mathcal R}B_n)\cong (P\otimes_{\mathcal R}Q)\otimes_{\mathcal R}B_n $$
sends $(p\otimes a)\otimes(q\otimes b)$ to $(p\otimes q)\otimes ab$, and its inverse sends $(p\otimes q)\otimes a$ to $(p\otimes1)\otimes(q\otimes a)$. The maps commute with differentials and quotient transitions. Tensor of two K-flat complexes is K-flat directly from its definition: tensoring an acyclic complex first with $Q$ and then with $P$ remains acyclic. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] identify the completed operation of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] with $C(A\otimes^L B)$, naturally in both variables. In particular its completion unit is the ordinary quotient unit, not an arbitrary lift to a Roos fiber.

source.place: Tags 06YU and 0G7E; balanced tensor reassociation followed by quotient completion

proof.text: Ordinary derived tensor is exact in each variable. Indeed represent a triangle by a cone of a map between flat-term K-flat complexes using the resolving equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]; its cone is still K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. Apply [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] to a fixed K-flat representative of the other argument: the image is its cone triangle, with the usual tensor shift signs. Restriction of scalars retains the underlying abelian sheaf, hence preserves kernels and cokernels [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Reduction and restriction of scalars therefore give an exact functor to the derived category of strict towers: at the representative level the quotient maps commute with all cone inclusions and projections. The exact $R\lim$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] shows that $C$ is exact, including its natural shift comparison. Hence $-\widehat\otimes^L M=C(-\otimes^L M)$ is exact. The unit $\eta$ commutes with shifts because its maps into every finite quotient do, and the same strict-tower functor gives its map into $R\lim$.

source.place: Tag 07A3 (tensor cone comparison); Tags 0940 and 0941 (exact derived inverse limit)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], $L\mapsto H(L,\mathcal R)$ and $L\mapsto H(L,M)$ send triangles to reversed distinguished triangles, with the contravariant shift comparisons $H(L[1],N)\cong H(L,N)[-1]$. Combining this with Step 3 proves exactness of $\Phi$ and $\Psi$. The scalar action on the derived category is the componentwise one of [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. Precomposing a map by $a f$ in either Hom model multiplies the resulting map by $a\in\mathcal O_E$; tensor and the tower maps do the same. Thus both functors are $\mathcal O_E$-linear, as are their shift comparisons. Step 1 converts the hypothesis on $M$ into local derived completeness; [lem-sf-ringed-rhom-derived-complete] then proves that $\Psi(L)=H(L,M)$ is derived complete for every $L$, including on a slice.

source.place: Tag 08JC (RHom triangulated), Tag 099A (algebraization.tex); linearity on complex representatives

proof.text:
Use the ordinary evaluation transformation of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps], with the Koszul symmetry to order the source as $H(L,\mathcal R)\otimes^L M$. Denote it by $e_L:H(L,\mathcal R)\otimes^L M\to H(L,M)$. Its adjunct evaluates the first Hom on $L$, then multiplies by $M$. Step 4 makes its target complete. Therefore the reflector property in Step 1 gives a unique map
$$\theta_{L,M}:C(H(L,\mathcal R)\otimes^L M)\longrightarrow H(L,M),\qquad\theta_{L,M}\eta=e_L.$$
This is the completed evaluation comparison of the statement by Step 2. For $f:L\to L'$, the two maps from $C(H(L',\mathcal R)\otimes^L M)$ to $H(L,M)$ obtained from the naturality square have equal precomposition with $\eta$, by naturality of $e$; the reflector bijection makes them equal. Thus $\theta$ is natural in $L$.

source.place: Tags 08JD, 08JE and 0A98 (ordinary evaluation); Tag 0A0E (algebraization.tex), uniqueness of completion extension

proof.text: Check shifts first for ordinary $e$, using the source order $M\otimes^L H(L,\mathcal R)$ of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]. Choose a K-flat complex $P$ for $L$, a flat-term K-flat $Q$ for $M$, and K-injectives $I_{\mathcal R},I_M$ for the two targets. Represent the canonical derived map $Q\otimes I_{\mathcal R}\to M$ by a chain map $u:Q\otimes I_{\mathcal R}\to I_M$; this is possible since the target is K-injective. The evaluation model sends $q\otimes\phi$ to $(x\mapsto u(q\otimes\phi(x)))$. For $\phi$ of Hom degree $a$, the comparison $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P[1],I)\to\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,I)[-1]$ sends $\phi$ to $(-1)^a\phi$, as follows by substituting into $d\phi=d_I\phi-(-1)^a\phi d_P$. For $q\in Q^b$, the tensor comparison $Q\otimes D[-1]\to(Q\otimes D)[-1]$ contributes $(-1)^b$. Thus shifting before evaluation contributes $(-1)^{a+b}$, exactly the Hom comparison after evaluation in degree $a+b$. This proves the shift square; the symmetry gives the same square in the source order of $\Phi$. Integer shifts follow by iteration and inversion. These identities descend from the representative models, so do not assume an equality of transformations merely from agreement on perfect generators.

source.place: Tags 08J9, 08JD and 0A98; Hom differential in Section 0A8X and total tensor signs

proof.text: Apply $C$ to the ordinary shift square of Step 6. By Step 3, the unit $\eta$ is compatible with the exact shift comparisons of $C$. The two sides of the desired completed shift square for $\theta$ are maps into the complete object $H(L,M)[-1]$; their precompositions with $\eta$ are the two sides of the ordinary square, hence equal. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] makes the completed square commute. Shifts of complete objects are complete: apply the vanishing condition in Step 1 and the shift formula of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Hence $\theta$ commutes with all integer shifts.

source.place: Tag 0A0E (algebraization.tex); Tag 08JC, completion extension and shifts

proof.text: By [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], a morphism in $\mathcal T[1/t]$ is a fraction $Q(f)/t^n$. For $F=\Phi,\Psi$, set $\overline F(L)=F(L)$ and $\overline F(Q(f)/t^n)=Q(F(f))/t^n$, reversing arrows. This is well defined: any equality of fractions becomes an integral equality after multiplication by a power of $t$, and Step 4 makes $F$ preserve that equality. Composition, identities and naturality of $Q\theta$ follow by the same fraction formula. The shift comparisons descend likewise. By [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated], every localized distinguished triangle is isomorphic to the image of an integral distinguished triangle. Step 4 sends the latter to a reversed distinguished triangle, so the descended functors are exact. Step 7 shows that $Q\theta$ is compatible with their shifts.

At $L=\mathcal R[0]$, evaluation at $1$ identifies $H(\mathcal R,N)$ with $N$: on a K-injective representative the map $\phi\mapsto\phi(1)$ has inverse $n\mapsto(r\mapsto rn)$ and commutes with differentials. Thus $e_{\mathcal R}$ is the unit action $\mathcal R\otimes^L M\to M$. Steps 1 and 2 identify $\theta_{\mathcal R,M}$ with $\eta_M^{-1}:C(M)\to M$, which exists by the completeness hypothesis on $M$. Hence $\mathcal R[0]\in\mathcal S_M$. The two functors take zero to zero and $\theta_0$ is its identity, so $0\in\mathcal S_M$.

Write $\alpha_L=Q\theta_{L,M}$. Naturality under an isomorphism identifies its two components by conjugating with the isomorphisms furnished by $\overline\Phi,\overline\Psi$, so membership is invariant under localized isomorphisms. Since these functors are additive, the inclusions and projections of a finite direct sum identify $\alpha_{A\oplus B}$ with $\alpha_A\oplus\alpha_B$; the inverse is $\alpha_A^{-1}\oplus\alpha_B^{-1}$. Step 7 identifies $\alpha_{L[n]}$ with $\alpha_L[-n]$ through the shift comparisons. This proves closure under finite sums and shifts in both directions.

source.place: Naturality, additive biproduct identities, and Step 7

proof.text:
Suppose $i:A\to B$ and $p:B\to A$ are morphisms in $\mathcal T[1/t]$ with $p i=1_A$ and $\alpha_B$ invertible. Contravariance gives $\overline F(i)\overline F(p)=1_{\overline F(A)}$ for both functors. Define
$$\beta_A=\overline\Phi(i)\,\alpha_B^{-1}\,\overline\Psi(p):\overline\Psi(A)\to\overline\Phi(A).$$
Naturality gives $\alpha_A\overline\Phi(i)=\overline\Psi(i)\alpha_B$ and $\overline\Psi(p)\alpha_A=\alpha_B\overline\Phi(p)$. Substitution shows $\alpha_A\beta_A=\overline\Psi(i)\overline\Psi(p)=1$ and $\beta_A\alpha_A=\overline\Phi(i)\overline\Phi(p)=1$. Thus $A\in\mathcal S_M$. This allows retract maps with denominators and assumes no integral splitting or ambient idempotent completeness.

Let $L_1\to L_2\to L_3\to L_1[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in $\mathcal T[1/t]$. Exactness gives the two reversed image triangles, with vertices $\overline\Phi(L_3),\overline\Phi(L_2),\overline\Phi(L_1)$ and the corresponding $\overline\Psi$ vertices. Naturality supplies the first two commuting squares, and shift compatibility supplies the last square (including its contravariant triangle sign). Consequently $(\alpha_{L_3},\alpha_{L_2},\alpha_{L_1})$ is a morphism of distinguished triangles. If two components are invertible, [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the third invertible. This proves the stated two-out-of-three extension property. Together with Steps 9–11 it proves every closure assertion for $\mathcal S_M$.

Added only the missing general Stacks 099A completeness lemma. The statement is unchanged.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q87-44cb5048d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node, every cited node, the unit, the parent and the cited Stacks places in full. New node lem-sf-ringed-rhom-derived-complete matches Stacks 099A (algebraization.tex) exactly, with local completeness as in Definition 0999, where T(K,f) is R Hom(O_f,K). It adds and drops no hypothesis, and K=0, N=0, I=0, I=O and the Z_p examples Q_p and a free sum are consistent. It is not a duplicate: lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction gives the same conclusion only on the global X_proet, while the item needs arbitrary slices; the reflector, Cech, restriction and flat-equivalence nodes do not state Hom preservation. The node has only a statement and the B fields are correct. Item steps: (1) O_E is a Noetherian DVR, so the constant-completion lemma, whose last paragraph covers Koszul and quotient completion for the completed sheaf, together with the reflector applies on slices. I checked that the Roos-triangle definition of completeness agrees with the local condition, through TR3 and invariance under isomorphism. (2) The balanced tensor identification gives completed tensor = C(ordinary tensor). (3) K-flat cones, the tensor cone identification and the exact strict-tower R lim (no product exactness needed) make C exact. (4) Internal Hom is exact with signed shifts, O_E-linearity holds componentwise, and the new node plus step 1 make Psi(L) complete. (5) theta is the unique map with theta eta = e, natural by the reflector bijection. (6) I re-derived the shift sign (-1)^(a+b); the evaluation model is internal composition, as in lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps. (7) The completed shift square holds because complete shifts are complete. (8) Fractions descend because the functors are O_E-linear, and exactness descends because every localised triangle is isomorphic to the image of an integral one. (9) For the unit, theta = e eta^-1, which uses completeness of M; with M=E on a point the map fails, so the hypothesis is needed. (10)-(11) Isomorphism, sum, shift and retract closure hold; I multiplied out the retract inverse. (12) Extension closure follows from 014A in T[1/t]. The statement is unchanged and serves the parent's steps 9-10 on slices. There is no cycle (766 nodes followed), no missing or merged citation, no SGA source, and proof_deps equals the union of uses. I accept all 10 off-route tool_uses as generic ringed-site tools; the unit's sentence on exact functors and direct summands is carried by steps 3-4 and 8-12. Minor: the step-8 source 05R6 and the step-3 source 07A3 are loosely placed but not wrong. I made no fixes.
